title: AnimationPlayer "Next (Auto Queue)" property is saved to scene file as empty string for animations in an Animation Library
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.5.stable.official [876b29033], 4.6.stable.official [89cea1439], 4.6.3.stable, v4.7.rc1.official [a4f5e8cdd] ### System information Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue, 02 Jun 2026 18:26:58 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 9070 (radeonsi, gfx1201, ACO, DRM 3.64, 7.0.11-arch1-1) - AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 30.45 GiB memory ### Issue description When set, the "Next (Auto Queue)" property for animations that are in an Animation Library is saved to the scene file as an empty StringName instead of the name of the animation that it should transition into. ### Steps to reproduce The MRP has a scene with an AnimationPlayer, AnimationLibrary and Animations already created, so you can skip to step 4 and select the "Library/LibraryAnim" animation in that step. Any other animation can be selected for step 5. From a new project: 1. Create a new scene with an AnimationPlayer in it 2. In the animation editor, create a new Animation Library: Animation > Manage Animations > New Library 3. Add 2 new animations, with at least one of them in the Animation Library: Animation > New > Select library from dropdown 4. Select the animation that is in the library from the animation dropdown 5. Set the Next (Auto Queue) for this animation to the other animation: Animation > Edit Transitions > Next (Auto Queue) 6. Save the scene, close it and reopen it 7. On reopening the scene, an error will be printed to Output: `ERROR: Animation not found: {LibraryName}.` where {LibraryName} is replaced with the name of the library 8. The animation's Next (Auto Queue) property will be blank, instead of being set to the animation that was set in step 5 9. If you open the scene .tscn file in a text editor, the AnimationPlayer node will have `next/{LibraryName}/{AnimationName} = &""` saved, with an empty StringName as the value instead of the name of the animation to transition to From my testing, this issue only happens when the animation on which the Next property is set is in an animation library. It doesn't matter if the animation that the property is set to is in a library or not, and setting the property to a library animation for a global (non-library) animation has no issue. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Godot version 4.6.3 [anim-next-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28737589/anim-next-bug.zip)
